title: Computer Concepts
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Outcome c (use a computer) is practical: the teacher watches the learner start up, open a program, save a file with a clear name and shut down, and marks it with the rubric. The questions test the knowledge behind each step.

skills.key_step: The learner explains data (raw facts) and information (processed data), and the characteristics of a computer: speed, accuracy (correct output from correct input), storage, diligence (works long hours without tiring), versatility (many kinds of jobs), automation (follows stored instructions).

floor.question: Name one way to collect data.

representations: a data to information arrow chart
characteristic cards with a picture each
a receipt printed from a till
steps: Explain wrong input gives wrong output.

board.say: Is this data or information, and why?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say information, it was processed.

listen_for: Data too, they are the same thing
misconceptions.ask: A list of marks 45, 62, 38 is data. What is the class average?
misconceptions.repair: Give raw marks (data), then work out the average together (information). Sort ten examples into data and information.

listen_for: The right price, computers never make mistakes
misconceptions.ask: A clerk types a wrong price. What will the computer print?
misconceptions.repair: Teach "garbage in, garbage out": type a wrong price on purpose and print the receipt.

listen_for: It gets tired and needs rest
misconceptions.ask: What does diligence mean for a computer?
misconceptions.repair: Say diligence means working for long hours without getting tired or bored; compare a cashier at the end of the day with a till.

misconceptions.ask: How does a computer know what to do?
misconceptions.repair: Follow a short program step by step on paper; show that the computer only follows the instructions given.

misconceptions.ask: Which characteristic means a computer can do many kinds of jobs?
misconceptions.repair: Show one computer doing a letter, a game, a calculation and a video call; name the characteristic versatility.

checks.question: A list of raw marks is data or information?
Which characteristic means a computer can do many kinds of jobs?

skills.key_step: The learner classifies computers by function (analogue, digital, hybrid), purpose (general purpose, special purpose) and size (supercomputer, mainframe, minicomputer, microcomputer, including laptops, tablets and smartphones).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the characteristics of a computer.
floor.question: Name one characteristic of a computer.

board.do: Draw a tree with three branches: function, purpose, size.

board.say: Which purpose group is it in?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say special purpose.
Fill in the tree with all the cards.

misconceptions.repair: List what a smartphone does (input, processing, storage, output) and compare with a desktop.

misconceptions.ask: Which is the biggest and most powerful type?
misconceptions.repair: Put the four on a size ladder (super, mainframe, mini, micro) with a picture and an example use each.

misconceptions.ask: What does an analogue computer work with?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a car speedometer needle (continuous) with a digital count; analogue computers measure continuous quantities.

misconceptions.ask: A computer in a washing machine does only one job. What type is it?
misconceptions.repair: List computers that do one job (washing machine, ATM, traffic light) and say they are built for that job.

checks.question: Is a smartphone a computer? Which size group?
A computer in a washing machine is general or special purpose?

skills.key_step: The learner gives the steps of a computer task in order (switch on, log in, open a program, work, save with a clear name in a chosen folder, close, shut down, then switch off at the socket) and says why each matters; the practical task is marked with the rubric.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parts of a computer.
floor.question: Which device do you use to point and click?

representations: a step strip: switch on, log in, open, work, save, close, shut down
a screenshot of the Save dialog with the name box circled
steps: Open a program by double-clicking its icon.
Save with a clear name in a chosen folder.
Close the program and shut down before switching off at the socket.
contexts: typing a club notice in the computer lab
saving a project to return to next week
a power cut in the middle of work

board.do: Write the steps on cards in the wrong order.
Point at the card "switch off at the socket".
board.say: Where does this card go, and what must come before it?

board.do: Wait for the learner to place it last, after Shut down.
Put all the cards in order and read them aloud.

listen_for: Switch it off at the wall socket
misconceptions.ask: You have finished working on a desktop computer. What do you do first?
misconceptions.repair: Show the Start menu and Shut down; explain that the computer must close its files first, or work and files can be lost or damaged.

misconceptions.ask: You type a letter and close the program without saving. What happens to the new work?
misconceptions.repair: Type one line, close without saving on purpose, reopen the file and see it gone. Then save and repeat.

listen_for: Click Save and keep the name Document1
misconceptions.ask: What should you do when you save a file for the first time?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the class to find "Document1" among twenty files with the same name. Then name files like "Kamau budget Term 1".

misconceptions.ask: How do you open a program from its icon on the desktop with a mouse?
misconceptions.repair: Practise: one click selects (the icon turns blue), two quick clicks open. Let the learner see the difference.

checks.question: What must you do before closing a program you have typed in?
What do you do before switching off at the socket?
